content.thinking: I've got a solid structure forming: starting with the foundational work from Ware in the '90s, moving through recent breakthroughs like the affordable webcam-based fish tank VR systems and holographic parallax displays that boost realism, then covering emerging approaches like Co-Globe's spherical setup and the 2025 light-field work with eye-tracking. From there I can build toward proposing novel directions that combine their Pepper's ghost technique with spatial audio, multi-viewer integral imaging, and deformation feedback to push the field forward. Recent work like Kim et al.'s holographic display system combines head-tracked motion parallax with accommodation cues, while spherical fish tank VR and commercial autostereoscopic systems with eye tracking represent current directions. The most promising unexplored territory would be systematically integrating spatial audio with head-tracked visual parallax to enhance depth perception, combining multi-user fish tank VR with personalized audio streams per viewer, or building a fully multimodal system that merges webcam tracking, deformable objects, contact sounds, and tactile feedback—most existing fish tank VR research focuses purely on visual aspects without exploring these audio-haptic combinations.

Fish Tank VR研究の系譜を、①黎明期の基礎研究、②発展・応用期、③最新の動向の3段階に分けて整理し、その上で新規性のある方向性を考察します。

## ①系譜：黎明期の基礎研究（1990年代〜2000年代前半）

**起点となる論文**
- **Ware, C., Arthur, K., & Booth, K. S. (1993)** *"Fish tank virtual reality"* — CHI'93/INTERACT'93
  「Fish Tank VR」という用語を作った原典。視点追従とステレオ立体視の両方を検証する3つの実験を行い、視点追従（ヘッドカップリング）はステレオ立体視より3次元性の強い印象を与える上でより重要である可能性を示唆したという結論が、その後の研究の出発点になった。

- **Arthur, K. W., Booth, K. S., & Ware, C. (1993)** *"Evaluating 3D task-performance for fish tank virtual worlds"* — ACM Transactions on Information Systems
  木構造のトレース課題において、頭部追従を用いたステレオ表示は、追従なしの静的な表示と比べて誤答率が一桁改善するという結果を示し、その効果はステレオ単体による効果より顕著だったという、Fish Tank VRの有効性を定量的に証明した基礎論文。

- **Deering, M. (1992)** *"High resolution virtual reality"* — SIGGRAPH
  CRTモニタを用いた頭部追従立体視システムの先駆け。当時のHMDの解像度不足問題を解決するために考案され、時分割方式の眼鏡と頭部トラッカーを組み合わせて、シームレスな運動視差と両眼視差を実現した。あなたの研究の「視点追跡による動的3D映像生成」と直接つながる技術的源流。

**発展・拡張期**
- **Ware, C. & Franck, G. (1996)** *"Evaluating stereo and motion cues for visualizing information nets in three dimensions"* — ACM Transactions on Graphics
- **Mulder, J. D. & Van Liere, R. (2000)** *"Enhancing fish tank VR"* — 画面端での負の視差を持つ物体の奥行き知覚の混乱を減らすため、カドル（額縁的な視覚的枠組み）表示や頭部回転の増幅表現などの技術を提案した
- **Arsenault & Ware (2000)** — 目と手の協調動作においては、頭部追従の視点よりもステレオ立体視のほうが重要であることを示した研究で、Wareら自身の初期結論を精緻化した
- Demiralp et al. — CAVEとFish Tank VRの科学的可視化タスクにおける有用性比較

## ②装置面での発展（多視点・裸眼化）

あなたの研究に近い方向性として、**Fish Tank VRの「頭部追従」原理を裸眼立体（オートステレオ）ディスプレイに組み込む**研究群があります。
- **"Interscopic User Interface Concepts for Fish Tank Virtual Reality Systems"** — 裸眼立体視ディスプレイ技術に基づく新しいユーザーインターフェース概念を導入し、モーショントラッキングとオートステレオディスプレイを組み合わせて3次元データの対話的な入力・操作を実現した研究。まさにあなたの「視点追跡＋裸眼立体＋インタラクション」という構成と一致する。

## ③最新の研究動向（2024〜2026年）

**低コスト・アクセシブル化の潮流**
- **"Real-Time 3D Light-field Viewing with Eye-tracking on Conventional Displays"**（2025, arXiv）
  標準的な2Dモニタと一般的なRGBウェブカメラ、赤青アナグリフメガネのみを使い、リアルタイムアイトラッキングでライトフィールド画像をユーザーの頭部位置に動的に適応させるシステムを提案し、CPUのみで30FPSの安定動作を実現した。あなたが使っているMediaPipeベースの視点追跡と発想が非常に近い、まさに「最新版Fish Tank VR」。

- ウェブカメラとMediaPipe Face Meshを用いた**オープンソースの頭部追従型視差ディスプレイ**の開発も2025年に活発化しており、MediaPipe Face Meshによる顔認識、座標変換、One-Euroフィルタによる平滑化、非対称視錐台計算を組み合わせ、Three.jsやCSSのperspective-originを通じて画面を物理的な窓のように振る舞わせる実装が公開されている。研究というより実装コミュニティの動きだが、技術トレンドとして重要。

**知覚的リアリズムの追求**
- **Kim, D. et al. (2024)** *"Holographic parallax improves 3D perceptual realism"* — ACM Transactions on Graphics
  ホログラフィックディスプレイに運動視差を統合し、より自然な奥行き知覚を実現する研究。従来のFish Tank VR（視差のみ）を、より高度な光学技術（ホログラフィ）と融合させる方向性。

**多人数・広視野角化**
- 2018年にSIGGRAPHで発表された「Co-Globe」は、球面の投影スクリーンを持ち、360度の視野角で運動視差と両眼視差を提供する、FTVRの発展形として紹介されている。

## 新規性があると考えられる研究方向

これまでのFish Tank VR研究を俯瞰すると、**「視覚（視差・立体視）」単体の最適化に研究が集中しており、あなたが取り組んでいる「聴覚（空間音響）」「触覚的な変形フィードバック」との統合的な検証はほぼ手つかず**です。具体的には：

1. **視点追従×空間音響の統合的な知覚評価**
Fish Tank VRの研究はすべて視覚的な運動視差・立体視の効果検証にとどまっており、頭部位置に連動した音源のHRTF制御を同時に組み込んで「視覚と聴覚の運動視差」を統合評価した研究は見当たりません。Ware(1993)の「視点追従はステレオより重要」という古典的知見が、聴覚的な奥行き手がかりを加えた場合にも成り立つのかは、まだ検証されていない問いです。

2. **複数人インテグラルイメージング×個別空間音響のマルチモーダル奥行き提示**
複数人が同時に異なる角度から立体像を見られる装置（インテグラルイメージング）に対して、各視聴者ごとに異なる方向から音が聞こえるような個別化された空間音響を重ねる研究は、管見の限り存在しません。「1人称のFish Tank VR」から「複数人称のFish Tank VR＋個別音響」への拡張は新規性が高いと考えられます。

3. **低コストWebカメラ式Fish Tank VR＋接触変形＋接触音のフルマルチモーダル統合**
最新の研究トレンド（MediaPipeベースの低コストFish Tank VR）と、あなたがすでに調査している「接触時の物体変形」「接触音による実物感向上」を、単一の安価な装置（Webカメラ＋ペッパーズゴースト）に統合した研究は見当たりません。既存研究は「視覚のみ」「触覚のみ」「音響のみ」を個別に評価する傾向が強く、これらを同一の裸眼立体装置上でシステム化し、SUS・NASA-TLX・Presence Questionnaireで統合評価するアプローチ自体が新規性を持ちうるでしょう。

4. **頭部追従データの二重利用によるパーソナライズドHRTF**
Fish Tank VRはもともと頭部位置をリアルタイムに取得しています。この既存のトラッキングデータを追加ハードウェアなしでそのままバイノーラル音響のHRTF制御にも転用し、個人化された立体音響を低コストで実現する、という技術的な統合は既存研究にあまり見られない着眼点です。

これらのうち、特に③（マルチモーダル統合の低コスト装置化）は、あなたのこれまでの研究の流れ（変形フィードバック、空間音響、裸眼立体、複数人視聴）を自然に統合する形になっており、卒業研究の新規性の主張として説得力を持たせやすいと思います。詳しく掘り下げたい方向があれば教えてください。

I've found some really promising papers on this topic—ImmersiveTouch stands out with its combination of a half-silvered mirror, head tracking, haptics, and spatial audio, along with related systems like the Responsive Workbench and VR-workbench. Now I'm pulling together the academic sources, particularly the ImmersiveTouch paper on designing high-performance haptic augmented reality systems.検索の結果、**ミラー反射型（ハーフミラー）× 頭部/視点追従（Fish Tank VR型）**を組み合わせた学術研究が複数見つかりました。特許文献も多くヒットしましたが、原著論文を中心に整理します。

## 主要な原著論文・学術研究

**1. Krüger, W., Bohn, C. A., Fröhlich, B., Schüth, H., Strauss, W., & Wesche, G. (1995)**
*"The Responsive Workbench: A Virtual Work Environment"* — *IEEE Computer*, 28(7), 42-48
ミラー反射型立体ディスプレイの古典的な原点。プロジェクタの映像をミラーで反射させて机型のスクリーンに投影し、シャッター眼鏡による立体視と頭部追従を組み合わせたワークベンチ型VRシステムを提案した。あなたの装置構成（ディスプレイ→ミラー反射→立体視）の技術的な源流にあたる研究で、Fish Tank VR系譜とミラー反射型立体ディスプレイ系譜が交わる重要な結節点。

**2. Banerjee, P. et al.（EVL, University of Illinois at Chicago）**
*"Design of the ImmersiveTouch: a High-Performance Haptic Augmented Virtual Reality System"*
ハーフミラー（半透過鏡）を使い、机型の作業空間の上部にディスプレイを配置してミラーに映像を反射させ、ユーザーの頭部・手を追跡することで視点連動の立体視と力覚提示を同時に実現する原著研究。**「頭部位置を追跡して視点連動の立体視を行うと同時に、その追跡データを使ってリスナー中心の3D音響もレンダリングできる」**と明記されており、あなたの「視点追跡＋空間音響の統合」という発想と直接一致する記述がある点が特に重要。

**3. VR-workbenchに関する医療応用研究**
半透過ミラーを用いたVRワークベンチにおいて、モニタから反射された仮想シーンと自分の実際の手を同時に見ることができる構成を用い、超音波診断や穿刺針の触診シミュレーションに応用した研究。CT画像から生成した患者の臓器モデルを表示し、視覚・触覚の統合レンダリング手法を検証している。

**4. Team-i3D (INRIA) の研究群**
*"Virtual Reality Configurations and Workbench"*
プロジェクタの映像をミラーで反射させてテーブル状のスクリーンに投影し、シャッター眼鏡による立体視と頭部追従を組み合わせる構成を報告。視覚化空間と操作空間（仮想・実空間）を頭部追従によって重ね合わせることで、より直感的なインタラクションを可能にすると論じている。

## 補足：特許文献（参考情報として）
検索では以下のような特許も多数ヒットしました。学術論文ではありませんが、装置設計の技術的な参考にはなります。
- *"Haptic augmented and virtual reality system for simulation of surgical procedures"*（半透過ミラー＋頭部追従による外科手術シミュレーション）
- *"Compact haptic and augmented virtual reality system"*（ミラーを45度に配置し、頭部・手のトラッキングと力覚デバイスを統合したコンパクトなデスクトップ型装置）

これらの特許の構成（ディスプレイを上部に配置し、45度のハーフミラーで下方の作業空間に虚像を投影する）は、あなたの装置の「天井型ディスプレイ配置＋斜め45度ハーフミラー」という構成そのものであり、権利関係の系譜として押さえておくと装置設計の妥当性を説明しやすくなります。

## サーベイ上のポイント
**ImmersiveTouch論文**が最も重要です。ミラー反射型立体ディスプレイ＋頭部追従に加えて、「同じトラッキングデータを用いてリスナー中心の空間音響も実現できる」と明言している点は、あなたの研究テーマ（視点追跡×空間音響の統合）が学術的にも自然な発展方向であることを裏付ける良い根拠になります。この論文のPDFを取得して詳しく読み込みますか？

content.title: Haptic augmented and virtual reality system for simulation of surgical procedures
content.text:

The display system of the open surgery station 10 can use a display screen 28 that can be a single passive stereo monitor, a half-silvered mirror 30 to reflect the image of the display screen 28, and a head tracking system 26 to display a dynamic viewer-centered perspective. The partially transparent mirror 30 can permit the user 12 to see both the virtual reality display and the user's hands, thus providing an augmented reality environment. The user can hold and manipulate the haptic device 22 with its stylus 27 below the mirror 30. The display system of the microsurgery station 11 can display a static perspective by using two display screens 28, which can be non-stereo monitors located side by side and a binocular surgical eyepiece 31, which can consist of four first-surface mirrors oriented at an angle in such a way that the image of the left monitor is only seen by the left eye, and the image of the right monitor is only seen by the right eye. 

The orientation and distance between the front-surface mirrors can be adjusted by the user to match his/her interocular distance. In the open surgery station 10, a virtual projection plane can be located exactly at the center of the haptic workspace and oriented perpendicular to that line, whereas in the microsurgery station 11 the user can view the virtual projection through the binocular surgical microscopic eyepiece 31. In the open surgery station 10 the partially transparent mirror 30 can preferably be sufficiently wide to allow the user to view virtual objects from different viewpoints (displaying the correct viewer-centered perspective) while permitting a comfortable range of movement. In contrast, in the microsurgery station 11, the binocular surgical microscopic eyepiece 31 can be adjusted up or down, either manually or by an automatic up-down adjustor, and the interocular distance can also be adjusted for comfortable 3-dimensional viewing.

content.title: ImmersiveTouch™ | 3D Systems
content.text:
ImmersiveTouch is the first system that integrates a haptic device with a head and hand tracking system and a high resolution high pixel-density stereoscopic display. Its ergonomic design provides a comfortable working volume in the space of a standard desktop.

ImmersiveTouch™ is the next generation of augmented virtual reality technology. ImmersiveTouch is the first system that integrates a haptic device with a head and hand tracking system and a high resolution high pixel-density stereoscopic display. Its ergonomic design provides a comfortable working volume in the space of a standard desktop. The haptic device is collocated with the high resolution 3D graphics, giving the user a more realistic and natural means to manipulate and modify 3D data in real time. Force feedback takes virtual reality beyond the visual to the tactile domain; from a limited interaction to a hands-on workbench for training and simulation. 

The high-performance, multi-sensory computer interface allows easy development of medical, dental, engineering or scientific virtual reality training applications that appeal to many stimuli: audio, visual, tactile and kinesthetic.

Unlike alternative systems, a real-time electromagnetic system tracks the user's head position and orientation to display the correct user-centered stereoscopic perspective. This guarantees that true graphics and haptics collocation is achieved even when looking at the 3D scene from different angles. In addition, hand tracking allows users to use both hands to interact with the virtual scene. While they can feel tactile sensations with the hand holding the haptic stylus, they can use the tracked hand to move the 3D objects, manipulate lights, or define clipping planes in the same 3D working volume. http://www.ivri.com http://www.immersivetouch.com Text and images are copyright Industrial Virtual Reality, Inc. ...

content.title: Development of MirrorShape: High Fidelity Large-Scale Shape Rendering   Framework for Virtual Reality
content.text:
## 2 PRINCIPLE AND TECHNOLOGIES

The MirrorShape system software consists of four modules (Figure 2), which includes Hand tracking module, VR environment, Robot controller and end-effector haptic display MirrorGlide.


Figure 2: The MirrorShape (a) software and (b) hardware architecture

The system hardware consists of a 6 DOF Universal robot UR3, PC with control framework, tracking system, and shape-forming end-effector (Figure 3) as haptic display. User wears HTC Vive Pro headset with Leap Motion camera to detect the position of the hands. The design of inverted five bar linkage mechanism allows MirrorGlide to define the position of 3 contact points independently, achieving a fairly wide range of the working area. The generation of 3 contact points combined with silicone display provides interaction with various shapes only with 3 DOF device instead of using large number of pins and actuators.

Projects video from the computer onto a mirror, which reflects the image onto the back of a large screen forming the workbench. The screen is a 4:3 aspect ratio, identical to the video monitor on the computer. The first workbenches oriented the screen horizontally.

Projects video from the computer onto a mirror, which reflects the image onto the back of a large screen forming the workbench. The screen is a 4:3 aspect ratio, identical to the video monitor on the computer. The first workbenches oriented the screen horizontally. Subsequent implementations of the idea have tilted the screen as much as thirty degrees. ... Use of LCD shutter glasses and a stereo projection mode can create a convincing three-dimensional effect. Most workbenches employe the use of tracked glove or wand systems for navigation. Some implementations use head tracking to further refine the stereoscopic effects. ... 

In a two-user Virtual Reality Responsive Workbench (VRRWB) system, both users are head-tracked using something like the Polhemus 3Space magnetic field tracking system. The system must correctly determine the two users' positions from the tracking hardware and compute four images - one for each eye of both users.

Dragon can drive CRT monitors, head mounted displays, the Virtual Reality Responsive Workbench, and the Graphical Room for Orientation, Training, and Tactical Observation (GROTTO.) Output of all devices can be in mono or stereo mode. Interface devices include keyboard, mouse, speech recognition, pinch gloves, tracked ``wands,'' and tracked head positioning. vrLib generalizes all input devices as 6DOF or TEXT virtual devices. In practice, gloves proved to be undesirable, and tracked wands were most effective. ... In all modes, simple text strings at the bottom center of the screen indicate recent changes, such as navigation mode.

summaries.summary: ミラー反射型立体ディスプレイの関連論文を収集中。

content.text:
検索の結果、**ミラー反射型（ハーフミラー）× 頭部/視点追従（Fish Tank VR型）**を組み合わせた学術研究が複数見つかりました。特許文献も多くヒットしましたが、原著論文を中心に整理します。

## 主要な原著論文・学術研究

**1. Krüger, W., Bohn, C. A., Fröhlich, B., Schüth, H., Strauss, W., & Wesche, G. (1995)**
*"The Responsive Workbench: A Virtual Work Environment"* — *IEEE Computer*, 28(7), 42-48
ミラー反射型立体ディスプレイの古典的な原点。プロジェクタの映像をミラーで反射させて机型のスクリーンに投影し、シャッター眼鏡による立体視と頭部追従を組み合わせたワークベンチ型VRシステムを提案した。あなたの装置構成（ディスプレイ→ミラー反射→立体視）の技術的な源流にあたる研究で、Fish Tank VR系譜とミラー反射型立体ディスプレイ系譜が交わる重要な結節点。

**2. Banerjee, P. et al.（EVL, University of Illinois at Chicago）**
*"Design of the ImmersiveTouch: a High-Performance Haptic Augmented Virtual Reality System"*
ハーフミラー（半透過鏡）を使い、机型の作業空間の上部にディスプレイを配置してミラーに映像を反射させ、ユーザーの頭部・手を追跡することで視点連動の立体視と力覚提示を同時に実現する原著研究。**「頭部位置を追跡して視点連動の立体視を行うと同時に、その追跡データを使ってリスナー中心の3D音響もレンダリングできる」**と明記されており、あなたの「視点追跡＋空間音響の統合」という発想と直接一致する記述がある点が特に重要。

**3. VR-workbenchに関する医療応用研究**
半透過ミラーを用いたVRワークベンチにおいて、モニタから反射された仮想シーンと自分の実際の手を同時に見ることができる構成を用い、超音波診断や穿刺針の触診シミュレーションに応用した研究。CT画像から生成した患者の臓器モデルを表示し、視覚・触覚の統合レンダリング手法を検証している。

**4. Team-i3D (INRIA) の研究群**
*"Virtual Reality Configurations and Workbench"*
プロジェクタの映像をミラーで反射させてテーブル状のスクリーンに投影し、シャッター眼鏡による立体視と頭部追従を組み合わせる構成を報告。視覚化空間と操作空間（仮想・実空間）を頭部追従によって重ね合わせることで、より直感的なインタラクションを可能にすると論じている。

## 補足：特許文献（参考情報として）
検索では以下のような特許も多数ヒットしました。学術論文ではありませんが、装置設計の技術的な参考にはなります。
- *"Haptic augmented and virtual reality system for simulation of surgical procedures"*（半透過ミラー＋頭部追従による外科手術シミュレーション）
- *"Compact haptic and augmented virtual reality system"*（ミラーを45度に配置し、頭部・手のトラッキングと力覚デバイスを統合したコンパクトなデスクトップ型装置）

これらの特許の構成（ディスプレイを上部に配置し、45度のハーフミラーで下方の作業空間に虚像を投影する）は、あなたの装置の「天井型ディスプレイ配置＋斜め45度ハーフミラー」という構成そのものであり、権利関係の系譜として押さえておくと装置設計の妥当性を説明しやすくなります。

## サーベイ上のポイント
**ImmersiveTouch論文**が最も重要です。ミラー反射型立体ディスプレイ＋頭部追従に加えて、「同じトラッキングデータを用いてリスナー中心の空間音響も実現できる」と明言している点は、あなたの研究テーマ（視点追跡×空間音響の統合）が学術的にも自然な発展方向であることを裏付ける良い根拠になります。この論文のPDFを取得して詳しく読み込みますか？

chat_messages.text:
I'm synthesizing across all the research elements they've discussed—the Fish Tank VR display with Pepper's ghost effects, spatial audio for depth perception, multi-viewer integral imaging, Leap Motion hand tracking with object deformation, and contact sound feedback—to identify where genuine novelty could emerge in combining these technologies together.

The key gaps seem to be in the integrated audio-visual-haptic experience: while individual components exist in literature, the specific combination of head-tracked spatial audio synchronized with motion parallax, visual deformation feedback, and contact sound in a multi-user Fish Tank VR context appears underexplored. I should frame concrete novelty positions around this integration—whether that's the perceptual effect of audio depth cues enhancing the visual parallax illusion, the haptic-audio feedback loop during object manipulation, or the multi-user spatial audio coordination—and assess which is most feasible given their 7-9月 implementation window and 10-11月 evaluation timeline.ここまで調べてきた内容を統合すると、新規性を狙えるポイントはいくつかの階層に整理できます。あなたの研究がすでに触れている要素（①視点追従×裸眼立体、②複数人立体視、③空間音響、④接触変形フィードバック）を軸に、既存研究が「手をつけていない組み合わせ」を探すのが最も現実的な戦略です。

## 新規性が見出せる可能性が高い順

**1. 視点追従（Fish Tank VR）×空間音響の統合検証 — 最有力**
これまでのFish Tank VR研究（Ware 1993以降）は一貫して「視覚（視差・立体視）」の効果検証にとどまっており、**頭部位置に連動した音源のHRTF制御を同時に評価した研究がほぼ存在しません**。唯一近いImmersiveTouchも「同じトラッキングデータで音響も出せる」と示唆するだけで、実際にその効果を測定してはいません。
→ 「視点追従による立体視だけの条件」と「視点追従立体視＋連動する空間音響を加えた条件」を比較し、Presence Questionnaireやobject realism評価で差を検証する、という実験デザインは、既存研究に穴があいている場所を正確に突いています。**理論的独自性が最も高く、実験デザインもシンプル**なので、B4後期の実験計画として最も着手しやすいと思います。

**2. 接触変形＋接触音の複合フィードバックによる実物感向上の定量評価**
笠井らの論文は変形フィードバックのみで、有用性評価実験自体がまだ行われていません（論文中でも「今後の課題」と明記）。一方、「Metal Sounds Stiffer than Drums...」は音のみで変形は伴わない実験です。
→ **変形フィードバックと接触音を組み合わせた条件」と「どちらか一方のみの条件」を比較する実験は、両者を橋渡しする位置にあり、まだ誰もやっていない組み合わせ**です。特に「音の周波数・減衰特性を変えることで、同じ変形量でも硬さ・実物感の知覚が変わるか」という軸は、既存の2つの研究をつなぐ新しい問いになります。

**3. 複数人立体視×個別空間音響（パーソナライズド音響）**
インテグラルイメージングによる複数人立体視の研究は視覚のみに閉じており、各視聴者に対して個別に方向付けられた音響（各人の頭部位置に応じた指向性のあるHRTF音響）を重ねる研究は見当たりません。ただしこれは**技術的難易度が高く**（複数人の頭部位置を同時トラッキングし、各人に別々の音を届ける必要がある＝スピーカーアレイやビームフォーミング技術が必須）、B4後期〜卒論の期間（7-12月）で実装まで持っていくのは難易度が高めです。将来の拡張方向として位置づけるのが妥当かもしれません。

**4. 低コストWebカメラ式装置への統合**
2025年のトレンドである「Webカメラ＋MediaPipeによる低コストFish Tank VR」に、あなたの研究要素（変形・接触音・空間音響）を統合するというのは、技術的にはあなたがすでに持っている構成（GPU付PC＋MediaPipe＋TouchDesigner）そのものです。**「安価な民生機材だけで、視覚・聴覚・疑似触覚を統合した裸眼立体インタラクションシステムを実現した」という点自体が、システム論文としての新規性**になり得ます（専用ハードウェア中心の先行研究〈ImmersiveTouchやResponsive Workbench〉との対比で語れる）。

## おすすめの絞り込み方

スケジュール（7-9月実装、10-11月実験・評価、12月論文執筆）を踏まえると、**①（視点追従×空間音響）を主軸に据え、④（低コスト統合システムとしての新規性）を装置面の売りとして添える**のが最も現実的だと思います。②（変形×音）はテーマとして魅力的ですが、すでに笠井論文が変形部分を扱っているため、あなたの研究では「空間音響」の比重を主軸にし、変形フィードバックは補助的な要素として位置づける、という役割分担にすると全体の一貫性が出ます。

どの方向で研究計画を具体化するか、一緒に実験デザインまで詰めていきましょうか？

Based on the novelty direction I identified around viewpoint tracking and spatial audio integration, I'm narrowing down which paper would be most useful as the primary source for this assignment. The Villegas & Cohen paper on virtual sound source localization in binaural reproduction seems like the strongest candidate since it directly addresses the spatial audio component that's central to that promising research direction. Zahorik's paper stands out because it directly addresses the audiovisual distance perception mismatch that's central to the proposed research direction, and it's packed with psychophysics terminology like visual capture and ventriloquist effect that would be valuable for vocabulary extraction. I should verify it's genuinely original research and confirm the citation details before finalizing this recommendation.これまでの議論を踏まえると、**①「視点追従×空間音響の統合」を主軸にする**という新規性の方向性が固まったので、この方向に最も直結する論文を選ぶのが合理的です。

## 最も有効な論文

**Zahorik, P. (2022)**
*"Asymmetric visual capture of virtual sound sources in the distance dimension"* — *Frontiers in Neuroscience*, DOI: 10.3389/fnins.2022.958577

### なぜこの論文が最適か

1. **あなたの研究の核心仮説と完全に一致している**
　視覚ターゲット（実際のスピーカー位置）と聴覚ターゲット（バイノーラル音源、1〜5m）の距離を意図的にずらし、視覚が聴覚の距離知覚をどの程度「捕捉（visual capture）」するかを実験的に検証した論文です。これはあなたが最初に紹介した関連研究[3]（視覚と聴覚の距離感情報を意図的にずらすことで奥行き知覚を音でコントロールする）と発想の根が同じであり、かつ「新規性①：視点追従×空間音響の統合」という今後の研究方向にそのまま接続します。

2. **原著論文として確実**
　n=11の被験者実験を実施し、心理物理学的手法（psychometric function）で視覚捕捉の非対称性を定量化した、査読付き実験論文です（既にこの会話内で確認済み）。

3. **未知語抽出の教材として質が高い**
　"visual capture"（視覚捕捉）、"ventriloquist effect"（腹話術効果）、"psychometric function"（心理測定関数）、"auditory distance perception"（聴覚的距離知覚）など、あなたの研究計画書や今後の論文執筆で必ず使うことになる専門用語が集中しています。単語を抽出すればそのまま卒論の理論的背景の語彙リストになります。

4. **要約が今後の「関連研究」節にそのまま使える**
　この論文を今要約しておけば、後期に書く卒論・学会論文の「関連研究」節の下書きとして転用できます。二度手間になりません。

## 次点candidate（参考）
もし技術実装寄りの語彙（HRTF補間、バイノーラルレンダリングの実装手法など）を優先したい場合は、**Villegas & Cohen (2015) "Locating virtual sound sources at arbitrary distances in real-time binaural reproduction"**（*Virtual Reality*誌）の方が実装面の専門用語密度が高く、システム構築段階（7-9月）で直接参照する機会が多い論文です。

**理論・仮説側を固めたいなら Zahorik (2022)、実装側を固めたいなら Villegas & Cohen (2015)** という使い分けになります。今の段階（7月、まだ研究テーマを固めている時期）であれば、前者から着手するのがおすすめです。

　視覚ターゲット（実際のスピーカー位置）と聴覚ターゲット（バイノーラル音源、1〜5m）の距離を意図的にずらし、視覚が聴覚の距離知覚をどの程度「捕捉（visual capture）」するかを実験的に検証した論文です。これはあなたが最初に紹介した関連研究[3]（視覚と聴覚の距離感情報を意図的にずらすことで奥行き知覚を音でコントロールする）と発想の根が同じであり、かつ「新規性①：視点追従×空間音響の統合」という今後の研究方向にそのまま接続します。

2. **原著論文として確実**
　n=11の被験者実験を実施し、心理物理学的手法（psychometric function）で視覚捕捉の非対称性を定量化した、査読付き実験論文です（既にこの会話内で確認済み）。

3. **未知語抽出の教材として質が高い**
　"visual capture"（視覚捕捉）、"ventriloquist effect"（腹話術効果）、"psychometric function"（心理測定関数）、"auditory distance perception"（聴覚的距離知覚）など、あなたの研究計画書や今後の論文執筆で必ず使うことになる専門用語が集中しています。単語を抽出すればそのまま卒論の理論的背景の語彙リストになります。

4. **要約が今後の「関連研究」節にそのまま使える**
　この論文を今要約しておけば、後期に書く卒論・学会論文の「関連研究」節の下書きとして転用できます。二度手間になりません。

## 次点candidate（参考）
もし技術実装寄りの語彙（HRTF補間、バイノーラルレンダリングの実装手法など）を優先したい場合は、**Villegas & Cohen (2015) "Locating virtual sound sources at arbitrary distances in real-time binaural reproduction"**（*Virtual Reality*誌）の方が実装面の専門用語密度が高く、システム構築段階（7-9月）で直接参照する機会が多い論文です。

**理論・仮説側を固めたいなら Zahorik (2022)、実装側を固めたいなら Villegas & Cohen (2015)** という使い分けになります。今の段階（7月、まだ研究テーマを固めている時期）であれば、前者から着手するのがおすすめです。

content.text:
Canales, Ryan; Normoyle, Aline; Sun, Yu; Ye, Yuting; Luca, Massimiliano Di; Jörg, Sophie (September 2019, ACM Symposium on Applied Perception 2019) In this work, we investigate the influence of different visualizations on a manipulation task in virtual reality (VR).

This reduced performance could be remediated with adequate visual feedback. In this study, we analyze the performance, level of ownership, and user preference of eight different visual feedback techniques for virtual grasping. Three techniques show the tracked hand (with or without grasping feedback), even if it intersects with the grasped object. Another three techniques display a hand without intersections with the object, called outer hand, simulating the look of a real world interaction. One visualization is a compromise between the two groups, showing both a primary outer hand and a secondary tracked hand. Finally, in the last visualization the hand disappears during the grasping activity.

In this study, we analyze the performance, level of ownership, and user preference of eight different visual feedback techniques for virtual grasping.

Ryan Canales, Yuting Ye, Aline Normoyle, Massimiliano Di Luca, Yu Sun, Sophie JörgSeptember 2019 ... In this work, we investigate the influence of different visualizations on a manipulation task in virtual reality (VR). Without the haptic feedback of the real world, grasping in VR might result in intersections with virtual objects. As people are highly sensitive when it comes to perceiving collisions, it might look more appealing to avoid intersections and visualize non-colliding hand motions. However, correcting the position of the hand or fingers results in a visual-proprioceptive discrepancy and must be used with caution. Furthermore, the lack of haptic feedback in the virtual world might result in slower actions as a user might not know exactly when a grasp has occurred.

content.title: SPHaptics: A Real-Time Bidirectional Haptic Interaction Framework for Coupled Rigid-Soft Body and Lagrangian Fluid Simulation in Virtual Environments
content.text:
Our approach integrates Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) with two-way force coupling and feedback smoothing to maintain stability and produce physically meaningful tactile responses. This enables users to manipulate objects immersed in fluid and feel reaction forces consistent with fluid-structure behavior. We demonstrate the capabilities of our framework through interactive VR scenarios involving fluid stirring, soft tissue manipulation, and rigid-body interaction. The proposed system advances hapticenabled multiphysics simulation by unifying fluid, soft-body, and rigid-body dynamics into a single platform suitable for immersive educational applications.

#### **Keywords**

Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics, Haptics, Real-Time Simulation, Virtual Reality, Education

## 1 Introduction

Haptic interaction has emerged as one of the key components of immersive and physically engaging virtual experiences. 

object immersion, drag, buoyancy, and deformation under flow, are inherently governed by the coupled dynamics of solids and fluids. Realistic simulation of these interactions requires consistent two-way coupling, in which the motion and forces of solid bodies influence the fluid flow, and vice versa. For virtual reality (VR) applications, this coupling must occur at real-time rates to maintain physical accuracy and responsiveness. Achieving this bidirectional interaction in real time remains a major challenge, since accurate fluid dynamics are computationally expensive while haptic feedback requires fast and stable force updates.

To address this, our work introduces a unified framework for bidirectional haptic interaction between rigid and deformable solids and Lagrangian fluid models, implemented within a real-time VR physics platform.

content.title: Grabity: A virtual reality haptic controller for creating gravity and stiffness during grasping motions through asymmetric vibrations
content.text: In this invention, we introduce Grabity, a mobile, ungrounded haptic device, which can display various types of kinesthetic feedback to enhance the grasping and manipulating of virtual objects. This feedback includes gravity, force for inertia, as well as rigid stiffness force feedback between opposing fingers. The design combines a “gripper” style haptic device, for providing opposing forces between the index finger and thumb, and a skin deformation mechanism, for rendering inertia and mass of a virtual object. Asymmetric skin deformation enabled by linear vibratory motors can generate perceived virtual forces tangential to finger pads. In this invention, we apply this principle to render the virtual gravity force of different virtual masses, and their associated inertia in a 1 degree of freedom per finger. To create the sensation of gravity and inertia, we adapt two voice coil actuators to a mobile gripper type haptic device.

name: お笑いサークル向けネタ見せフォーム作成アプリ
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation involved building a Google Forms automation tool for a Japanese comedy circle (お笑いサークル) to streamline the creation of "ネタ見せ" (performance showcase) feedback forms. The person is a circle organizer who previously created these forms manually each time—a tedious process involving entering performer names, embedding YouTube links, and adding comment fields for each act. The goal was to fully automate this process so that entering basic information and pressing a button would create a complete Google Form.

The project evolved significantly over the course of the conversation. It began as a standalone HTML copy-paste helper tool, then pivoted to a Google Apps Script Web App after determining that actual form creation required Google authentication. The project consists of two files: `Code.gs` (server-side logic) and `index.html` (the client UI).

content.text:
1	---
     2	name: frontend-design
     3	description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
     4	license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Frontend Design
     8	
     9	Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.
    10	
    11	## Ground it in the subject
    12	
    13	If the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before – use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
    14	
    15	## Design principles
    16	
    17	For web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.
    18	
    19	Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
    20	
    21	Structure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.
    22	
    23	Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.
    24	
    25	Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
    26	
    27	Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
    28	
    29	## Process: brainstorm, explore, plan, critique, build, critique again
    30	
    31	For calibration: AI-generated design right now clusters around three looks: (1) a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta accent; (2) a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
    32	
    33	Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.
    34	
    35	Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.
    36	
    37	When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.
    38	
    39	Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.
    40	
    41	## Restraint and self-critique
    42	
    43	Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
    44	
    45	## More on writing in design
    46	
    47	Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
    48	
    49	Write from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.

    51	Use active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: "Save changes," not "Submit." function createForm(row) { // create from name "Name_Email_AppointmentDate" const formName = `${row[1]}_${row[2]}_On: ${row[6]}_At: ${row[7]}`; const formFolder = DriveApp.getFolderById(FORM_FOLDER_ID) // create forms in specific folder const form = FormApp.create(formName); // set title of the form form.setTitle("Preleminary Appointment Questions") // add questions from sheets const questions = JSON.parse(row[9]); questions.forEach(item => form.addParagraphTextItem().setTitle(item)); const file = DriveApp.getFileById(form.getId()); file.moveTo(formFolder); // console.log(form.getPublishedUrl()) // console.log(form.getId()) // create shareable link to the form accessible for the users gmail only with getPublishedUrl() return [form.getPublishedUrl(), form.getId()]; } ... The row parameter represents a specific row within the Appointments worksheet tab containing the ChatGPT-generated questions.

Let me parse the user's request carefully (it's spoken/dictated Japanese with filler words "えっと", "えー" - speech-to-text style, a bit broken).

Key points:
1. When adding to the performer list, they want to just paste the YouTube link (URL only), and the app should automatically fetch the YouTube video's title (which equals the performer's stage/group name, since that's their convention) and use that as the name. So: input simplifies to "just paste YouTube URL" → app auto-fills the name field by fetching the video title from YouTube.
2. They confirm: "今の段階では、まだフォームを作ることができない状態ですか" - asking confirmation that currently the form can't yet be created (i.e., still needs setup). They want to proceed to make it actually work - i.e., now let's go through the setup steps to get to a working state.

So two things to do:
A) Modify the app: performer list input changes from "name + URL" to "just URL" (paste link), then auto-fetch YouTube title via YouTube's oEmbed API or noembed, and use it as the name. Need also to keep ability to edit/override the name in case the auto-fetched title isn't exactly what they want (e.g robustness), but primary flow: paste URL → name auto-populates.

This requires fetching YouTube video metadata. Within Apps Script (Code.gs runs server-side in Google's infrastructure), we can use UrlFetchApp.fetch to call YouTube's oEmbed endpoint: https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=<video_url>&format=json - this returns JSON including "title" field, no API key required! This is the simplest approach, no need for YouTube Data API key setup. Let's implement a server function `fetchYoutubeTitle(url)` that calls oEmbed and returns the title, called from client via google.script.run when the URL field changes/blurs, or when bulk-pasting just URLs.

But there's nuance: oEmbed title field returns the exact YouTube video title (could contain extra stuff beyond just the group name, e.g if title is "ネタ見せ「残機」" or similar, but based on the original form, the hyperlinked text for each question was exactly the group name itself - implying these YouTube video titles are literally just the group/individual name, e.g. video titled "残機". So oEmbed fetch should usually return exactly the name. Good - using oEmbed title directly as performer name is reasonable. Allow user to edit afterward if needed.

B) For the bulk-paste feature: now they only need to paste YouTube URLs (one per line), no name needed since name auto-derives from title. Let's redesign:
- Single add: "＋1組追加" creates a row with just a URL input; once URL entered (on blur/input debounce), call server to fetch title, auto-fill name field (which remains editable e show fetched name).
- Bulk paste: textarea where they paste multiple YouTube URLs (one per line) → on "リストに反映", parse each URL, create rows, and for each, asynchronously fetch the title via the server function and populate.

Let's design the row UI: each performer row could show:
- order number
- URL input (primary entry point)
- name field (read-only display once fetched, but editable in case oEmbed fails or title needs tweaking) — readonly didn't matter, keep editable text input but auto-filled
- a small status/spinner while fetching
- remove button

Layout: order | URL input | name (auto, editable) | remove button - similar to before but now URL comes first, and name is auto-derived showing "取得中…" while loading.

Actually simplest UX matching their words "URLを貼るだけで名前が出るようにしたい": Maybe the row should just have a single URL input, and below/beside it show the fetched name as a label (not editable) plus a small "編集" affordance if needed. But for robustness, I'll keep name editable but default it to the fetched title, and visually indicate it was auto-filled (e.g., placeholder note "（YouTubeタイトルから自動取得）"). Let's design with a "URL" field primary, and "名前（自動取得・編集可）" field secondary that's populated automatically but stays editable.

Implementation:

Client side - when URL input loses focus (blur event) or after typing pause, and the URL field is non-empty and changed, trigger google.script.run.fetchYoutubeTitle(url) -> on success fill name field if name field is empty or matches previous auto-filled value (to avoid overwriting a manual edit unintentionally). I'll track each row's "autoName" flag: if the name field currently equals the last auto-fetched value (or is empty), overwrite with new fetched value; if user manually edited name (differs from last autofetched), don't overwrite automatically - but actually simplicity: just overwrite name whenever URL changes and fetch succeeds, since starting flow is "paste link only" anyway. To keep it simple per the user's stated mental model (paste link, name comes out), I will auto-fill name on every successful URL fetch, and still allow editing afterward (manual edits stay until URL changes again triggering a new fetch overwrite) - that's acceptable trade-off, mention this behavior briefly is not necessary, just make it work.

Bulk paste: redefine to accept just URLs (one per line). After parsing the list of URLs into rows (name initially blank, status "取得中..."), call fetchYoutubeTitle for each in sequence (or Promise.all-like via multiple google.script.run calls - need careful handling because google.script.run isn't promise-based natively; can wrap in a Promise for convenience).

Let's also keep support for pasting "URL <tab> custom name" for cases they want to override, but default expectation is just URL. I will design bulk parse: if line has a tab/multiple space-separated parts, treat first as name override... wait no, original was "name URL"; now there's no name needed. Let's just treat each non-empty line as a URL (trim, extract URL via regex matching http(s) part in case there's trailing text), and ignore everything else. Simpler. I'll add a small hint: "1行に1つのYouTubeリンクを貼ってください。"

Now implement server-side fetchYoutubeTitle(url):

```js
function fetchYoutubeTitle(url) {
  if (!url) throw new Error('URLが空です');
  var oembedUrl = 'https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=' + encodeURIComponent(url) + '&format=json';
  var res = UrlFetchApp.fetch(oembedUrl, { muteHttpExceptions: true });
  var code = res.getResponseCode();
  if (code !== 200) {
    throw new Error('YouTubeの情報を取得できませんでした（URLを確認してください）');
  }
  var data = JSON.parse(res.getContentText());
  return data.title || '';
}
```

This requires Apps Script to have external request capability (UrlFetchApp) - this is a built-in Apps Script service, no extra setup or scope registration needed beyond the standard authorization (Apps Script auto-detects required scopes from code, in this case https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.external_request, which is automatically requested during the OAuth consent screen along with Forms scopes; the user just approves once at deployment/first run). Good, no extra setup overhead like API keys.

Now let's update both files accordingly: Code.gs needs new function fetchYoutubeTitle; index.html needs UI/JS overhaul for the performer list.

Also: bulk-paste should call fetchYoutubeTitle for each URL - might hit Apps Script execution time limits if many URLs (but only ~13, fine). Each google.script.run call has overhead (~0.5-2s), so fetching 13 titles sequentially could take ~10-20 seconds; might want a combined server function that accepts an array of URLs and returns array of titles in one round-trip to reduce latency: `fetchYoutubeTitles(urls)` looping server-side and returning results array. That's more efficient - one round trip instead of N. I'll implement that for bulk-paste, and keep single fetchYoutubeTitle for individual row entry (or just reuse the bulk one with array of 1).

Let's design final Code.gs:

```js
function fetchYoutubeTitles(urls) {
  return urls.map(function(url) {
    try {
      var oembedUrl = 'https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=' + encodeURIComponent(url) + '&format=json';
      var res = UrlFetchApp.fetch(oembedUrl, { muteHttpExceptions: true });
      if (res.getResponseCode() !== 200) {
        return { url: url, title: '', error: 'タイトルを取得できませんでした' };
      }
      var data = JSON.parse(res.getContentText());
      return { url: url, title: data.title || '', error: null };
    } catch (e) {
      return { url: url, title: '', error: 'タイトルを取得できませんでした' };
    }
  });
}
```

This single function handles both single-row addition (call with array of 1) and bulk paste (call with array of N). Good, simplifies client code to one server call pattern.

Now update index.html:
- Remove old two-column row (name+url) replaced with: URL input prominent, name shown below/beside as auto-filled editable field, plus a status indicator (spinner / "取得中…" / error message inline if oEmbed failed, in which case ask them to type name manually).
- Add row UX: when "+1組追加" clicked, add an empty row with just URL field; when URL input blurred (or paste event) and non-empty, trigger fetch.
- Bulk paste: textarea now expects just URLs (one per line); on apply, parse lines into URLs (extract URL substring), create rows with name='', status='loading', then call fetchYoutubeTitles with all URLs at once, populate names array-wise by matching URL/index, set status done.

Let's write the row rendering: row layout grid-template-columns: order | URL input | name field (auto, editable, possibly with small "auto" badge) | remove button. We'll keep order: 26px, url input ~1fr, name input ~1fr, remove 32px. Should be fine on mobile (small screens) - might stack, but that's existing pattern (not stacking currently; rows have 4 columns and at narrow widths might get cramped). Given original design didn't have mobile stacking for performer-row (no media query for that), it's already imperfect on very narrow viewports but acceptable for now; I won't redesign mobile stacking unless asked, though I could quickly add a mobile breakpoint to stack url/name fields vertically for usability. Let's add a media query: at narrow width, change performer-row to two-row grid: first row is order+url+remove, second row is name field full width. That's a nice touch matching the "needs to look fine on phone" expectation since they're dictating via voice (likely on mobile?). Let's add this responsive tweak as a quality improvement, consistent with frontend-design skill's "responsive down to mobile" floor.

Now let's also address: "今の段階では、まだフォームを作ることができない状態ですか。これをフォームを作る状態に進めてください。" → they want to proceed to the setup steps now (deploy to Apps Script) so it actually works. So in this response I should:

2. Provide the step-by-step setup/deployment instructions to actually get the app live and working (since they explicitly asked to proceed to that point).

## セットアップ手順（最初の1回だけ）

**1. Apps Scriptプロジェクトを作る**
[script.google.com](https://script.google.com) を開き（Googleにログインした状態）、「新しいプロジェクト」をクリック

**2. サーバー側コードを貼る**
左側に最初からある `コード.gs`（または`Code.gs`）を開き、中身を全部削除して、上の **Code.gs** の内容を貼り付ける

**3. 画面側コードを追加する**
左側の「ファイルを追加」（＋ボタン）→「HTML」を選択 → ファイル名を `index` にする（拡張子は自動でつきます）→ 中身を全部削除して、上の **index.html** の内容を貼り付ける

**4. プロジェクト名をつける**
左上の「無題のプロジェクト」をクリックして、好きな名前に変更（例：ネタ見せちゃん作成）

- Access: Anyone with a Google account

Given their message: "サークルの人がおのおののアカウントで使用できる効率化アプリ" — "each person can use [the creation tool] with their own account" — this clearly means (a): multiple people should be able to use the CREATION tool itself, each authenticated as themselves, presumably because duty rotates among members for different ネタ見せ days.

Given that, Option A (Execute as: User accessing the web app, Access: Anyone with Google account) is the right fit, but I should clearly flag the unverified-app-warning friction as the cost of this architecture, and present alternatives:

**Option C: Google Workspace Marketplace / verified app** — too heavy, requires actual Google verification process (weeks, business justification, privacy policy, etc.) — total overkill for a casual comedy circle, not recommended.

This still requires authorization per user on first run (same "unverified app" warning) — that friction is unavoidable with any custom Apps Script regardless of hosting context, since it stems from OAuth scope consent, not the URL/hosting method. This is a nice complementary feature suggestion but doesn't eliminate the verification-warning friction.

**Option E: True client-side standalone HTML + OAuth (the original idea explored earlier)** — Requires hosting on a stable origin and OAuth client ID setup in Cloud Console. This was already discounted as heavier than Apps Script. 1. Affirm that Apps Script is still the right base technology (no need to switch to something totally different)
2. Explain the one key setting change needed: Execute as → User accessing the web app, Access → Anyone with Google account
3. Explain the trade-off/friction (everyone sees the unverified app warning once)

いい質問です。今の構成（Apps Script Web App）自体は土台として正しいです。サークルメンバー全員が使えるようにする場合に直すべきは「**デプロイの設定**」だけで、技術を全部入れ替える必要はありません。ただ、地味だけど無視できないトレードオフが1つあるので、それを踏まえて方向を決めたいです。

## 今の構成のままで複数人対応する方法

設定を2か所変えるだけです。

| 項目 | 今の設定 | 変更後 |
|---|---|---|
| 次のユーザーとして実行 | 自分 | **ウェブアプリにアクセスしているユーザー** |
| アクセスできるユーザー | 自分のみ | **Googleアカウントを持つ全員** |

「実行するユーザー」を本人に変えることで、誰が開いても**その人自身のGoogleアカウントでフォームが作られる**ようになります（他の人のフォームが自分のDriveに作られたりしない）。前回作った「前回の出演者リストを覚えておく」機能も、この設定なら**人ごとに別々に記憶される**ので、むしろ都合がいいです。

## トレードオフ（ここが重要）

この設定にすると、**メンバー1人ひとりが、初回利用時に「Google hasn't verified this app」のあの警告を自分で1回クリックして突破する**必要があります。私が今回あなたと一緒に乗り越えた手順を、メンバー全員が最初の1回だけ踏むイメージです。技術に慣れていないメンバーだと「なんか怖い」と離脱してしまう可能性があります。

## 代替案：作成役は数人だけに絞る

もし実際の運用が「基本的には決まった1〜2人（あなたや副担当）がネタ見せ回ごとにフォームを作る」というものなら、今のままの「自分のみ」設定で、**その1〜2人だけが使うツール**にしておくのも十分合理的です。他のメンバーは今までと同じく、出来上がったフォームのリンクを受け取って回答するだけなので、見え方は変わりません。この場合、警告を見るのはあなた含む数人だけで済みます。

どちらが実際の運用イメージに近いですか？

Unfortunately, the service account cannot directly execute Google Apps Script by the current specification. However, fortunately, the Web Apps can be accessed by the service account. This workaround uses this situation. The key factor for this workaround is to use the Web Apps deployed as Execute as: Me and Who has access to the app: Anyone with Google account. The service account is used for firing the Web Apps and the script of Google Apps Script is run as the owner of the Google Apps Script project (It's you.). You can see the figure of this as shown in the above figure. For example, when the Web Apps deployed as Execute as: Who has access and Who has access to the app: Anyone with Google account is used, the service account cannot access the Web Apps. Of course, it is considered that it is possible to use the Web Apps as the wrapper API of Google Apps Script API.

On the script editor, at the top right of the script editor, please click "click Deploy" -> "New deployment". Please click "Select type" -> "Web App". Please input the information about the Web App in the fields under "Deployment configuration". Please select "Me" for "Execute as". Please select "Anyone with Google account" for "Who has access". Please click "Deploy" button. Please run the function getUr() of the above script. By this, you can see your Web Apps URL. It’s like https://script.google.com/macros/s/###/dev. Please copy this URL. This URL is used on the client side. If the URL is not dev, please retrieve it on the script editor. In this case, the Web Apps is accessed as the developer mode with the endpoint of https://script.google.com/macros/s/###/dev. So, when you modify the Google Apps Script, it is not required to redeploy Web Apps.

「デプロイを管理」の「アクセスできるユーザー」のところは、実は**個別に「○○さんと△△さんだけ許可」のような細かい指定はできません**。選べるのはこの3択です。

|---|---|
| 自分のみ | あなただけ |

| 全員（匿名含む） | ログイン不要の誰でも（※フォーム作成権限のような重要な権限を使うアプリでは選べないことが多いです） |

つまり「あなた＋数人だけ」をきっちり指定する設定はApps Script自体には無いので、現実的な対応は次の2つです。

**おすすめ：「Googleアカウントを持つ全員」にして、URLを教える人を絞る**
- 設定上は「誰でも」になりますが、実際にはURLを知っている人（＝あなたが個別に教えた数人）しか使いません
- 各自、初回だけ「Google hasn't verified this app」の警告を一度クリックする必要があります（あなたが最初にやったのと同じ操作）

これはバグではなく、複数のGoogleアカウントへの同時ログイン（マルチログイン）はApps Scriptのウェブアプリでは仕様上サポートされていないことが原因です。直すには、通常のSafariで一旦Googleから完全にログアウトしてから、使いたい1アカウントだけでログインし直してください（前回お伝えした「設定→Safari→履歴とWebサイトデータを消去」が確実です）。プライベートブラウズか、ログインしなおした通常ブラウザのどちらかで運用する形になります。

content.title: Troubleshooting | Apps Script | Google for Developers
content.text:
If you open a web app or add-on and experience multi-login issues, try one of the following solutions: Log out of all your Google Accounts and only log in to the one that has the add-on or web app you want to access.

Beyond explicit error messages, subtle errors can cause unexpected results, requiring debugging techniques like logging, checking executions, or using the debugger with breakpoints. Issues can also arise from exceeding service quotas, temporary server unavailability, insufficient authorization, domain policies restricting services like Drive API, problems with user identity access, missing or deleted libraries, or using multiple Google Accounts simultaneously. Even the most experienced developer rarely writes code correctly on the first try, making troubleshooting an important part of the development process. This section covers techniques to find, understand, and debug errors in your scripts. When your script encounters an error, an error message appears with a line number. There are two basic types of errors: syntax errors and runtime errors. Syntax errors occur when code doesn't follow JavaScript grammar and are detected when you save the script.

Triggers that fire before authorization or after expiration often cause this error. If an add-on causes this, use the add-on again to re-authorize. Remove problematic triggers: In the Apps Script project, click Triggers alarm. Next to the trigger, click More more_vert > Delete trigger. Alternatively, uninstall the add-on. Other actions, such as a user selectively denying required scopes during authorization on a surface that supports granular permissions, can also cause these errors. If a script runs in the background (such as on an installable trigger) and tries to use a service that the user did not authorize, it fails immediately. See the authorization scopes page to learn how to protect trigger executions. Google Workspace administrators can disable the Drive API for their domain, which prevents users from using Drive apps or Apps Script add-ons that use the Drive service.

This error occurs when a script attempts to call the .constructor property on a function (including async functions). Apps Script blocks this call to prevent the dynamic creation of new functions from strings (e.g., func.constructor('code')()), which is a security measure. ... Avoid creating functions from strings: Do not use the .constructor property to dynamically construct or invoke functions. Instead, define functions using standard function declarations. Some errors are subtle and don't trigger messages. For example, your code might be able to execute, but the results are unexpected. Use the following strategies to investigate scripts that behave unexpectedly. Record information as a script executes using the Cloud logging service or the Logger and console services in the script editor. If your administrators have turned on advanced settings for data regions, and some of your scripts were created before 2018, you might see a message indicating that Cloud Logging is stopped for the

However, this error continues to appear as long as the execution remains within the scope of the dynamic script. After execution moves out of the dynamic script, debugging continues without this error. If you're logged into multiple Google Accounts at the same time, you might have trouble accessing your add-ons and web apps. Multi-login, or being logged into multiple Google Accounts at once, isn't supported for Apps Script, add-ons, or web apps. If you open the Apps Script editor while logged in to more than one account, Google prompts you to choose the account you want to proceed with. If you open a web app or add-on and experience multi-login issues, try one of the following solutions: Log out of all your Google Accounts and only log in to the one that has the add-on or web app you want to access. Open an incognito window in Google Chrome, or an equivalent private browsing window, and log in to the Google Account that has the add-on or web app you want to access.

Now, the architecture question: can the Google Forms API/FormApp service create a "single item" that combines a video AND a text question together visually? Let's think about Google Forms' actual capabilities.

Google Forms structurally consists of a flat list of "items" (Form Item types): Video Item, Text Item, Paragraph Text Item, Section Header, Page Break, Image Item, etc. There's no native "combo item" that bundles a video + a question into one visual block/card. However, Google Forms DOES render each item as its own separate card/box in the UI by default. So strictly speaking, "1つの枠にまとめる" (combining into one single box/frame) literally is NOT possible via Forms' standard rendering — each Item (video, section header, question) gets its own separate visual card with spacing between them. This is a Google Forms platform limitation, not something we can change via the API/FormApp.

Let me reconsider the original form fetched at the very beginning of conversation — that original form had: question title = performer's name as a hyperlink, immediately followed by a comment text field per question — that was actually using ONE item per performer! Because in that legacy form, the performer's name (as a hyperlinked title) WAS the question title for the comment textbox itself — i.e ONE combined item: "title = [performer name as link]" + "answer = comment box". That's literally a single Text/Paragraph question item per performer, where the title IS the name+link, eliminating the need for two separate items (video item + question item).

But we moved away from that design because Forms API doesn't support embedding a clickable hyperlink within the question title text (confirmed earlier). So we switched to using a Video Item (separate item) to embed the actual playable video, followed by a separate paragraph question. This necessarily creates TWO items per performer instead of one, since Video Item and Question Item are fundamentally different Item types in the Forms data model, and you can't attach a "question/answer" to a Video Item directly.

So the honest technical answer is: **Google Forms doesn't support visually merging a video + a question into a single box.** Each item (video, question) is always rendered as its own separate card by the Forms UI; this is a platform-level constraint, not a limitation in our code. We cannot make them "look like one block" through the API.

Google Forms has "Section" breaks (which create distinct pages/sections in the form, separated by a header+page break) - not a tight visual grouping of a single video+question into one card; sections are for breaking the whole form into multiple pages, this is too heavy/wrong granularity for "per performer" grouping (would create 13 separate pages, awkward).

content.text:
1	---
     2	name: frontend-design
     3	description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
     4	license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Frontend Design
     8	
     9	Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.
    10	
    11	## Ground it in the subject
    12	
    13	If the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before – use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
    14	
    15	## Design principles
    16	
    17	For web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.
    18	
    19	Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
    20	
    21	Structure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.
    22	
    23	Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.
    24	
    25	Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
    26	
    27	Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
    28	
    29	## Process: brainstorm, explore, plan, critique, build, critique again
    30	
    31	For calibration: AI-generated design right now clusters around three looks: (1) a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta accent; (2) a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
    32	
    33	Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.
    34	
    35	Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.
    36	
    37	When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.
    38	
    39	Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.
    40	
    41	## Restraint and self-critique
    42	
    43	Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
    44	
    45	## More on writing in design
    46	
    47	Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
    48	
    49	Write from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.
    50	
    51	Use active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.
    52	
    53	Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.
    54	
    55	Keep the register conversational and tuned: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each element do exactly one job. A label labels, an example demonstrates, and nothing quietly does double duty.
    56

content.title: How to Get All URLs from a YouTube Playlist Without Scraping or Coding
content.text:
We already did all the hard work of managing API keys, handling complex pagination loops, and formatting the data. ... Go to your YouTube playlist and copy the URL from browser. Open our website and paste the URL in the box.

Now, if you are a software engineer or a technical person, your mind will say, "I don't need a scraper, I will just use the official YouTube Data API and write my own Python or Node.js script to get the links." Yes, you can do it. But ask yourself a simple question: is it really worth your time? Think about the steps involved. First, you have to go to Google Cloud Console. Then you have to create a new project, enable YouTube Data API v3, and generate API keys. Then you open your code editor, install libraries, and write the code. YouTube API does not give all videos in one single request. They give maximum 50 results per page. So you have to write a pagination loop to handle the nextPageToken just to get all the links. All this setup and coding will easily take 2 to 3 hours of your day. Your actual goal was just to get those video URLs so you can finish your data entry or analysis.

Our tool runs on the official YouTube API in the backend. It means it is 100% compliant with YouTube rules and totally safe. We already did all the hard work of managing API keys, handling complex pagination loops, and formatting the data. ... Go to your YouTube playlist and copy the URL from browser. Open our website and paste the URL in the box. Click the "Extract Links" button. In just one or two seconds, the tool will fetch all the URLs, whether it is 50 videos or 5000 videos. It will show everything in a clean table format on your screen. From there, you can just click the "Copy All" button to copy all raw links directly to your clipboard. Or, if you prefer, you can hit "Export As" and download everything directly into an Excel or CSV file. It is very straightforward. There is no signup required and the tool is completely free. We use the Official YouTube API to get the work done & we never do anything beyond YouTube guidelines.

So, you look for an automated way. If you search online, you will mostly see two pieces of advice: either scrape the webpage or write a custom code using the API. I am going to tell you practically why both these methods are actually bad ideas, and how you can get your work done in two seconds without doing any of that. The first shortcut people try is web scraping. They will install some free scraper extension in Chrome or try to write a quick script using tools like Python BeautifulSoup to read the webpage HTML. Please do not do this. First of all, scraping data is strictly against YouTube Terms and Conditions. YouTube is owned by Google, and they have world-class security engineers. Their server systems can easily detect when a bot or automatic script is trying to read their pages. If you try to run a scraper, they will quickly throw a block on your IP address.

An RSS reader could also subscribe to YouTube channels and playlists because YouTube supported RSS feeds initially. Go to https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=CHANNEL-ID, where CHANNEL-ID is the YouTube channel's ID (not the personalized URL). To find a YouTube channel's ID, right-click anywhere on the channel and select "View page source." The keyboard shortcut is Ctrl + u on Windows and ⌘ + Option + u on Mac. chat_messages.text:
理由を確認すると、実は「絶対に避けたい」という強い理由があったわけではありません。経緯を振り返ります。

最初に自動作成全体を検討し始めた段階で、**OAuthクライアントID方式**（素のHTMLアプリを独立したWebアプリとしてホストし、Googleの認証を直接組み込む方式）を検討した際に、その方式だと「Cloud Consoleでのプロジェクト作成・OAuthクライアントID発行・ホスティング・承認済みオリジンの登録」という**4ステップが必要**になり、これが「少し技術的」「やや手間が重い」という理由で、より簡単な**Google Apps Script（`FormApp`）方式**に切り替えました。

つまり「Cloud Consoleを避けたい」というのは、**OAuth認証を自前で組むこと自体を避けたい**という文脈での話で、「Apps Scriptの中で、YouTube Data APIという公式の高度なサービスを1つ有効にする」のとは、必要な作業量がかなり違います。

playlistItem resources contain properties like snippet for basic details, contentDetails for video-specific information, and status for privacy settings. The snippet property contains information on the item's title, description, position, thumbnails, the channels associated to it, and the resource included in the playlist. A playlistItem resource identifies another resource, such as a video, that is included in a playlist. In addition, the playlistItem resource contains details about the included resource that pertain specifically to how that resource is used in that playlist. YouTube also uses a playlist to identify a channel's list of uploaded videos, with each playlistItem in that list representing one uploaded video. ## 反映手順

今回は新しいGoogleサービス（YouTube Data API）を使うので、**1ステップだけいつもより多い**作業があります。

1. Apps Scriptエディタを開く
2. **左メニューの「サービス」の横にある＋ボタン**をクリック
3. 一覧から「**YouTube Data API**」を探してクリック → 「追加」
4. `Code.gs`を上の最新版で置き換えて保存
5. `index.html`も上の最新版で置き換えて保存
6. 「デプロイ」→「デプロイを管理」→鉛筆アイコン→「新バージョン」にして「デプロイ」
7. アプリを開き、出演者リストの項目の下にある「**再生リストから一括取り込み**」を試す

いい質問です。2つとも整理して答えます。

## 「誰が」許可する必要があるのか

これは**デプロイの設定によって変わります**。今回のアプリは「アクセスしているユーザーとして実行」という設定にしてあります（サークルメンバーそれぞれが、自分のGoogleアカウントでフォームを作れるようにするためでした）。この設定の場合、**権限の許可は「アプリを使う人ごと」に必要**です。つまり、

- **あなた**がフォームを作る分には、あなたが1回許可すればOK
- もし**別のメンバー**が初めてこのアプリを使ってフォームを作る場合、そのメンバー自身のGoogleアカウントで、同じような許可画面がそのメンバーに対して出ます（あなたが代わりに許可することはできません）

なので厳密には「スクリプトを作った本人だけが許可すればいい」わけではなく、**使う人それぞれが、自分のアカウントで初回に1回だけ許可する**という仕組みです。ただし、これは「YouTube機能を初めて使うとき」だけの話で、フォーム作成自体（Drive・フォームの基本機能）は、前回すでにDrive権限を許可したときに一緒に許可されている可能性もあります。

## 「前はできてたのに、今回はエラーが出た」の意味

これはおそらく、**Drive機能を許可した時点（前々回）では、まだYouTubeプレイリスト機能自体をコードに追加していなかった**ためです。時系列としてはこうです。

1. Drive機能を追加 → 権限確認 → 許可 →「フォーム作成＋Drive移動」は動くようになった
2. その後、YouTubeプレイリスト機能を**新たに追加**
3. YouTubeプレイリスト機能は、Driveとは**別の種類の権限**（YouTubeの読み取り）を必要とする
4. この新しい権限は、まだ誰も許可していなかったので、使おうとした瞬間にブロックされた

content.text:
いい質問です。2つとも整理して答えます。

## 「誰が」許可する必要があるのか

これは**デプロイの設定によって変わります**。今回のアプリは「アクセスしているユーザーとして実行」という設定にしてあります（サークルメンバーそれぞれが、自分のGoogleアカウントでフォームを作れるようにするためでした）。この設定の場合、**権限の許可は「アプリを使う人ごと」に必要**です。つまり、

- **あなた**がフォームを作る分には、あなたが1回許可すればOK
- もし**別のメンバー**が初めてこのアプリを使ってフォームを作る場合、そのメンバー自身のGoogleアカウントで、同じような許可画面がそのメンバーに対して出ます（あなたが代わりに許可することはできません）

なので厳密には「スクリプトを作った本人だけが許可すればいい」わけではなく、**使う人それぞれが、自分のアカウントで初回に1回だけ許可する**という仕組みです。ただし、これは「YouTube機能を初めて使うとき」だけの話で、フォーム作成自体（Drive・フォームの基本機能）は、前回すでにDrive権限を許可したときに一緒に許可されている可能性もあります。

これはおそらく、**Drive機能を許可した時点（前々回）では、まだYouTubeプレイリスト機能自体をコードに追加していなかった**ためです。時系列としてはこうです。

1. Drive機能を追加 → 権限確認 → 許可 →「フォーム作成＋Drive移動」は動くようになった

3. YouTubeプレイリスト機能は、Driveとは**別の種類の権限**（YouTubeの読み取り）を必要とする
4. この新しい権限は、まだ誰も許可していなかったので、使おうとした瞬間にブロックされた

つまり「時間が経って急に動かなくなった」のではなく、「新しく追加した機能が、まだ誰も通っていない新しい関門を持っていた」というのが正しい理解です。決して不安定になったり、突然壊れたりしたわけではありません。

name: 動画編集マニュアルの構成と進め方
summary:
**Conversation overview**

The person is a member of a university comedy circle called P-RITTS (千葉大学お笑いサークル P-RITTS) working on the circle's editing team (編集隊). They asked Claude to collaboratively plan and create a video editing manual for their team, intended for members with little to no experience using video editing software. The manual covers editing comedy live footage shot on and off campus for YouTube publication, using Adobe Premiere Pro (primary) and DaVinci Resolve (free alternative). The entire planning and drafting process was conducted through iterative conversation where Claude asked clarifying questions before each section, then presented draft content for approval or revision.

The conversation involved extensive content gathering about the circle's specific editing workflow: two types of editing exist (opening video with performer introductions, and main footage editing); main editing involves audio processing (multiband compressor with broadcast preset → hard limiter at -6dB → manual level adjustment via Effect Controls), handling dark stage transitions by lowering clip opacity to 9% (not 0%, to avoid looking like a frozen video) using a 4-keyframe pattern (100→9→9→100), cutting performer changeover gaps over 30 seconds with Cross Dissolve and Constant Gain/Crossfade 0dB audio transitions, and trimming head/tail footage. The manual also covers YouTube upload procedures with a specific description template format (learned from the person's actual uploaded screenshot: title format "〇月ライブ「サブタイトル」第〇部", with timestamps by 芸名/performer stage name set before ガナリ, and a Chiba University co-op Adobe student discount workflow). The person specified that Chiba University students can access Adobe CC at a discounted rate through the university co-op using their @chiba-u.jp email address, and that costs are covered by club expenses requiring coordination with the representative. Large file transfers must use Gigafile or wired connection (not LINE/email) to preserve video quality.

Claude built the manual iteratively across six parts (はじめに, オープニング編集ガイド, Premiere Pro本編編集ガイド, DaVinci Resolve本編編集ガイド, YouTubeアップロード手順, 困ったときに), generating a Word (.docx) file using Node.js with the docx library, with helper functions for headings, numbered/bulleted lists, callout boxes, screenshot placeholders, code blocks, and data tables. The person then completed the manual themselves by inserting real annotated screenshots and making text refinements (adding the P-RITTS circle name, adjusting opening video timing guidelines, adding "基本は触らなくて良し" to export settings, changing timestamp recording to happen post-edit using voice dictation on smartphone memo app with AI cleanup of full-width punctuation artifacts). **今の方法（素材自体の不透明度を下げる）**
シンプルで分かりやすい方法ですが、いくつか弱点があります。

- 毎回その素材自体のプロパティを操作するので、後で別のエフェクト（トランジションなど）を同じ素材にかけたい時に設定が混在してやりづらい
